***
## Campbell's groups

Building on Schulze's (1917) idea that hydra can be clustered into morphological types, Campbell (1987) established four groups of hydra: the **Viridissima group** (green hydras), the **Braueri group** (gracile hydras), the **Oligactis group** (stalked hydras) and the **Vulgaris group** (common hydras). Campbell summarized the distinct morphological traits of these groups into an identification key. In the same paper, Campbell described a new species, *H. lirosoma*, collected from a creek near the Okefenokee Swamp in southern Georgia, USA. 

Although Campbell placed *H. lirosoma* in the Braueri group due to the broad shape of its holotrichous isorhiza nematocysts, he noted that it differs from other group members *"by virtue of its spherical embryotheca, other species usually have flattened embryothecae that adhere to the substratum."*  Subsequent genomic characterization indicates that *H. lirosoma* actually represents an entirely distinct group of hydra. The identification key below has been modified from Campbell (1987) to reflect this updated taxonomic status.

It is important to note that **Campbell's groups** were comfirmed to correspond to monophyletic groups (clades) of hydra (Martínez et al. 2010). 

## Key to hydra clades

<div class="tax-key">
  <dl>
    <dt>1a.</dt>
    <dd>Hydra green due to intracellular algal symbionts;  <br>
    stenotele nematocysts not longer than 11 µm ........................................ <strong>Viridissima group</strong></dd>
    
    <dt>1b.</dt>
    <dd>Hydra not green; stenotele nematocysts longer than 11 µm</dd>
  </dl>

  <dl class="level-2">
    <dt>2a.</dt>
    <dd>Holotrichous isorhiza nematocysts plump (at half as broad as long)</dd>
  </dl>

  <dl class="level-3">
    <dt>3a.</dt>
    <dd>Flatten embryotheca without spines ............................... <strong>Braueri group</strong></dd> 
    <dt>3b.</dt>
    <dd>Round embryotheca with spines .................................... <strong>Lirosoma group</strong></dd>
  </dl>

  <dl class="level-2">
    <dt>2b.</dt>
    <dd>Holotrichous isorhiza slender, or if plump then embryotheca with spines</dd>
  </dl>

  <dl class="level-3">
    <dt>4a.</dt>
    <dd>Buds acquire 2 lateral tentacles before other tentacles appear;<br> 
    otherwise, stenoteles at least 1.5 times as long as broad <br>
    smooth, spherical embryotheca ..................................... <strong>Oligactis group</strong></dd>
    <dt>4b.</dt>
    <dd>Buds acquire tentacles in some other order; otherwise, <br>
    stenoteles less than 1.5 times as long as broad <br>
    spherical embryotheca with spines.................................. <strong>Vulgaris group</strong></dd>
  </dl>
</div>
